title: tenant-headroom-staleness-triggering-soft-throttles-during-burst-windows
creator: Marco Chen
description: Customer BrightMed reported recurring 429/slow responses during morning burst windows when their reserved pool should have absorbed load. Traffic patterns matched previously supported burst behavior but requests were soft-throttled for 10-20s while the autoscaler appeared healthy. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a short-term hotfix to prevent further customer-impacting throttles.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use tenant BrightMed in us-west-2 dedicated pool with burst credits near zero; 2) Replay traffic spike from 08:30-09:00 UTC using production traffic trace; 3) Observe request admission and warmup events; 4) Verify tail latencies and 429 rates against allocator/scale-controller logs.
logs_summary: Allocator shows lease extensions but no aggressive new allocations for 09:00 spike. Scale-controller metrics: warmup_eligible=true but warmup_completion_count remains zero for several minutes. Headroom_fingerprint metric drifted between replicas causing stale eligibility checks. Admission controller applied soft throttle policy when perceived headroom < threshold despite free GPU slots present.
mitigation_actions: 1) Immediate: increase tenant-specific soft-throttle threshold for BrightMed to avoid enforcement during morning windows (manual override applied 2026-03-11 14:10 UTC). 2) Deploy guardrail to skip soft-throttle enforcement for tenants with recent successful warmups until fingerprint sync is confirmed (hotpatch rolled 2026-03-12). 3) Add alert on headroom_fingerprint_staleness > 30s.
temporary_workarounds: - Customer can switch to a pinned dedicated pool for critical windows (ops-assisted). - Applied a manual warmup prefill for BrightMed for next 72 hours via reservations-engine command.
root_cause_summary: Race between scale-controller warmup epoch advancement and allocator fingerprint propagation: when the scale-controller marks a pool as warmup_eligible, allocator replicas occasionally laged (~20-45s) in fingerprint updates due to batching optimization introduced in runtime-1.20. During that window the admission policy saw inconsistent headroom and applied soft throttles even though physical capacity was available, causing customer-request surface 429s and latency spikes.
qa_checks: - Integration test: inter-replica fingerprint propagation under high update rates. - Load test: replay BrightMed morning burst trace with new guardrail enabled. - Regression: ensure batching optimization does not reintroduce >10s fingerprint lag.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary hotfix in us-west-2 small subset (10% traffic) for 3 hours. 2) Monitor headroom_fingerprint_staleness, admission_throttle_rate, tail latencies. 3) If stable, gradual rollout to all regions over 6 hours. 4) Post-rollout: enable fingerprint-propagation telemetry at higher cardinality for 72h.
stakeholders: Customer Success: Aisha Patel; Eng oncall: Liam O'Connor; SRE: Daniel Kim; Product: Sofia Martinez; Solutions Eng: Priya Rao (assignee)
communication_notes: - 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC: CS informed BrightMed of temporary override and manual prefill. - 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC: ops notified customer of hotpatch schedule and expected monitoring window. - Prepare a customer-facing summary once RCA confirmed.
next_steps: 1) Merge allocator and scale-controller PRs and coordinate canary with SRE (owner: Priya). 2) Implement permanent fix: reduce batching window for fingerprint propagation and add per-replica heartbeat. 3) Expand telemetry to surface headroom_fingerprint divergence by tenant. 4) Draft postmortem summary for customer and internal review.
notes: This issue differs from previous burst-accounting gaps: here physical GPUs were free but control-plane staleness caused admission decisions to be conservative. Long-term solution must balance propagation cost vs correctness.
